The Gitea provider works with gitea.com and self-hosted Gitea instances. It shares its implementation with the [Forgejo](/providers/forgejo) provider, so the Forgejo page applies here too, apart from the default instance, the webhook headers and CI. Refs from this provider have `forge: 'gitea'`.

## Authentication

The provider accepts an access token:

```ts
import { gitea } from 'forges/gitea'

const forge = gitea({
  auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.GITEA_TOKEN! },
})
```

If you leave out `auth`, the provider makes anonymous reads of public data.

## Instance

The default instance is `https://gitea.com`. To use a self-hosted instance, set `baseUrl` to the root of the instance. The provider appends `/api/v1` itself:

```ts
gitea({ baseUrl: 'https://gitea.example.com', auth })
```

`refreshCapabilities()` reads the version of the instance from `/version`.

## Review replies

`replyToReviewComment()` needs Gitea 1.27 or later. It replies by the comment's `ref`, and the reply joins the same review. gitea.com runs a recent build, so it works there out of the box. For a self-hosted instance, pass `instanceVersion` or call `refreshCapabilities()` first.

## Moderation

`threads.lock()` needs Gitea 1.24 or later, and sends the reason as one of the defaults of Gitea's `LOCK_REASONS` setting, such as `Too heated`. `orgs.block()` and `users.block()` need Gitea 1.22 or later. gitea.com runs a recent build; for a self-hosted instance, pass `instanceVersion` or call `refreshCapabilities()` first. Gitea has no API to hide a comment.

## Checks and CI

`checks.list()` reads commit statuses, and `checks.report()` writes them.

The `ci` methods read Gitea Actions. Runs and their jobs need Gitea 1.25 or later, job logs need Gitea 1.24, and `ci.rerunFailed()` needs Gitea 1.26. gitea.com runs a recent build, so they work there out of the box. For a self-hosted instance, pass `instanceVersion` or call `refreshCapabilities()` first.

Gitea 1.25 is stricter about the list of runs: it shows it only to the owners of the repository and to site admins, and responds with `403` to anyone else. From 1.26, everyone who can read the repository can list its runs. Without a token, Gitea responds with `401` to the list of runs and to job logs, so an anonymous provider can read a run and its jobs, but not list runs or read logs.

Gitea before 28 doesn't say when a run was created, so `createdAt` is unset there.

## Webhooks

To verify deliveries, set `webhookSecret` to the secret that you configured on the hook:

```ts
const forge = gitea({
  webhookSecret: process.env.GITEA_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
})

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

With each delivery, Gitea sends these headers:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Gitea-Signature` | The hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body |
| `X-Gitea-Event` | The event name |
| `X-Gitea-Delivery` | The delivery ID |

Unlike the Forgejo provider, the Gitea provider doesn't read `X-Forgejo-*` headers.

A label delivery doesn't say which labels were added or removed. When the set of labels changes, the provider reports a `label` event with the `edited` action, and when every label is removed, a `label` event with the `unlabelled` action.

## Organisation teams

`orgs.teams()` reads `GET /orgs/{org}/teams`, and `orgs.teamMembers()` reads the members of one team. Gitea addresses a team's members by id, so the provider reads `GET /teams/{id}/members` with the ref's `id`. For a ref with only a `slug`, it first resolves the slug (a team's name) to its id with the teams listing. Both need a token with the `read:organization` scope, and Gitea responds with a 403 when the account isn't a member of the organisation. A slug that names no team rejects with `NotFoundError`.
